articles.title: Plans for Demolition of Flats in Lower Falinge Resurface
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has revealed new plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, sparking distress among remaining residents.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has announced plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, which contain 126 homes, as part of a redevelopment project. The proposal aims to replace the existing structures with 270 new homes, including a mix of flats and houses, on land between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street.

The maisonette blocks known as Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, and Vaynor are set for demolition, with only the Zedburgh block currently occupied. Andy Roche, a resident since 1988, and his partner are the last remaining tenants in the Zedburgh block and have expressed their distress over the news. Roche stated, "I am not happy about RBH’s proposals, but I’m not sure how to put it into words. My partner is also distraught. We are both autistic and this eviction is making us both really ill."

The plans come after a successful legal challenge last year that halted previous demolition efforts. RBH claims the blocks are no longer fit for purpose and have exceeded their lifespan. The housing provider has stated that the new plans have been informed by consultations with local residents, although Roche feels that the voices of current tenants have not been adequately considered.

The estate has seen significant changes over the years, with previous demolition work leading to the construction of 100 new homes since 2012. However, Roche laments the loss of community, noting that many families have left the area, leaving behind a desolate landscape. The new proposals will likely mean further upheaval for the remaining residents as the redevelopment progresses.
